request.spec:
Show the duplicate claims: for each person, date and amount with two or more claims (VOID and
DELETED claims left out), one line <name> <date> <amount> x<count>, people in list order, then by
date, then by amount.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show the duplicate claims: for each person, date and amount with two or more claims (VOID and
DELETED claims left out), one line <name> <date> <amount> x<count>, people in list order, then by
date, then by amount.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The sheet now has a "Duplicate claims" panel, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

Press **Show duplicates** (`dups-show`) and it lists one `dup-line` for each person, date and amount that has two or more claims, as `<name> <date> <amount> x<count>`. VOID and DELETED claims are left out. People come in list order, then each person's lines are sorted by date, then by amount from lowest to highest. Once shown, the list keeps itself current as claims change, for example after a delete or a merge.

I only touched the front end, in one new file: `src/main/frontend/features/claims/dups.slot.tsx`. The screen already loads every person and claim on the sheet, so the panel works the list out from that. The server, stored data and audit file are unchanged; the test expects no new audit record for this.
